summary: San Dimas sits right where the San Gabriel Valley's suburban floor buckles upward into the foothills, which means the northern half of town tilts into genuine canyon terrain — Bonelli Regional Park alone covers over 1,900 acres of chaparral-draped hills with a reservoir, equestrian trails, and direct access to the San Dimas Experimental Forest — while the southern stretches flatten into standard grid neighborhoods along Arrow Highway and the Metrolink station. That transit link matters: this is largely a bedroom community, with most wage earners commuting west toward downtown Los Angeles or into adjacent cities along the I-210 and I-10 corridors, and the median household income of roughly $106,000 lands in a tricky spot against a median home value north of $756,000, putting the price-to-income ratio around 7.1 — manageable by greater-LA standards but far from comfortable. The old downtown strip along Bonita Avenue has a handful of sit-down restaurants, a few coffee spots, and an independently operated weekly farmers' market, giving the commercial core just enough gravity to feel like its own place rather than a freeway-adjacent afterthought. With 9.4 hours of daily sunshine on average and daytime highs that hover in the mid-70s year-round, the climate genuinely rewards the foothill trail access. San Dimas is essentially a place where proximity to wild, hilly open space and a Metrolink commute substitute for the urban density and walkability it plainly lacks.
